name: Pharmacy
title: At the pharmacy (lekarna)
character: a friendly pharmacist at a neighbourhood pharmacy (lekarna) in Ljubljana
setup: You are a friendly pharmacist at a neighbourhood lekarna in Ljubljana. A foreigner who is just starting to learn Slovenian has come in with a headache to get something for it. They live here and want to practice.
opening: Dober dan! Kako vam lahko pomagam?

objectives.label: Greet
objectives.hintEN: Beginners reach for the informal 'Zdravo' to a stranger; with a pharmacist it's the neutral 'Dober dan.'

objectives.label: Say what hurts
objectives.hintEN: English speakers calque the subject and say 'Moja glava boli' (or word-order-slip to 'Glava me boli'); in Slovenian the body part is the nominative subject and the person is the accusative clitic: boli ME glava.

objectives.label: Tablets, please
objectives.hintEN: Beginners reach for the cognate 'pilule' (or answer in English); the native word for over-the-counter pills is 'tablete'. Answering the binary 'Tablete ali sirup?'.

objectives.label: Ask price
objectives.hintEN: Ask the price — a real exchange; the pharmacist answers with the cost. Just the question; do not bundle the goodbye onto it.

objectives.label: Pay & leave
objectives.hintEN: One-breath closing as you leave. Said on its own, not crammed onto the price question.

sentences: Prideš v lekarno in rečeš: »Dober dan.«
Boli te glava, zato poveš: »Boli me glava.«
Lekarnarka vpraša: »Tablete ali sirup?«, in ti rečeš: »Tablete, prosim.«

frames.imagePrompt: Viewpoint from INSIDE the room looking toward the entrance: {{CUSTOMER}} stands in the open {{DOORWAY}}, framed by it, facing the viewer and waving as they step in over the threshold — the moment of arriving and greeting, seen from within the room they are entering.

{{CUSTOMER}} pressing one hand to the side of her forehead with a pained, wincing expression, a few small radiating ache-lines at her temple localising the hurt to her HEAD — the unmistakable look of a headache, not a stomach- or throat-ache.
A single blister pack of {{TABLETS}} — round white pills in a clearly-pilled silver foil sheet, unmistakably tablets as opposed to a bottle of liquid syrup. The 'tablets' form is the point.
A single {{PRICE_TAG}} showing a large question mark '?' — the concept of asking how much it costs (a question, not a fixed price).

{{CUSTOMER}} stepping OUT through the {{DOORWAY}}, facing away with an over-the-shoulder wave — the moment of leaving and saying goodbye. The outward direction (leaving, not entering) is what makes this a farewell.

story.sceneImagePrompt: At a {{LEKARNA}}: {{PHARMACIST}} stands behind the counter and {{CUSTOMER}} stands in front of it, the two turned toward each other across the counter in a natural exchange; a pack of {{TABLETS}} and {{EURO_COINS}} on the counter between them, with easy space around them.
